items.title: What Tata Trusts’ suits in Bombay High Court say against N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment
items.summary: Trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) have filed a suit before the Bombay High Court challenging a board resolution passed by Tata Sons Private Limited on September 17. That resolution has sought to reappoint Natarajan Chandrasekaran as the Executive Chairman of Tata Sons for another five years. The resolution was passed 4:1. Directors Venu Srinivasan, Harish Manwani, Anita M George and Saurabh Agrawal voted in favour. Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata voted against it while Chandrasekaran abstained. Tata Trusts, which controls 66% stake in Tata Sons, has argued that the reappointment resolution is void ab initio. They have sought a declaration that the resolution is ultra vires the Articles of Association and, hence, null and void. It has sought an order to restrain the company from acting on the reappointment. SDTT has also sought a bar on the board chair casting vote when 2 trust nominees disagree. Relief has been sought ahead of the November 30 board meeting. The trusts have collectively sought damages to the tune of ₹65 crore: ₹50 crore by SDTT, and ₹15 crore by RDTT. items.title: Saket court acquits former My FM CEO of sexual harassment charges
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Harish M Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, of the charges of outraging and insulting the modesty of a woman. Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of Saket courts held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Court reiterated that a conviction in a sexual offence can be based solely n a complainant's testimony only if the same is of sterling quality. "The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence," it said. Where the case rests primarily on that testimony, the Court must scrutinize it with greater care to ensure that it is free from material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities, the judge added. Since the same was not satisfied in the present case, Bhatia was acquitted of all charges. The complainant, then National Programming Head, alleged harassment between 2008 and 2010 at the workplace, office parties and tours.
